extracted.intended_audience: medical/public-health administrators, government policymakers, and practicing scientists concerned with scientific administration and sanitary policy
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for how government and medical administrations should organise, support, recognise, and act on scientific research—especially in tropical medicine and public sanitation; also criteria for industrial cooperation in lamp manufacture discussed in a technical-news context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of microscopes and bacteriological apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopes and bacteriological apparatus were generally wanting, although they are absolutely necessary in tropical clinical practice for the detection of numerous parasites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as an essential minimum resource requirement for effective tropical clinical practice; absence is treated as a major administrative failure (cited Army Medical Department report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental leaders must keep abreast of recent scientific advances
rubrics_metrics.description: The heads of the department frequently showed ignorance of recent scientific advances, as was apparent from their antiquated statistical methods and regulations for dealing with epidemics and their general lack of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should use up-to-date statistical methods and current scientific knowledge when framing regulations and epidemic responses; ignorance at the top leads to systemic failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of Service should distinguish real scientific and professional ability
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual 'Records of Service' of officers... was a hopelessly stupid form which made no attempt to distinguish their real scientific and professional ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel-evaluation forms and promotion records must capture substantive scientific/professional contributions rather than rely on superficial metrics that favour patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt official follow-up and scrutiny of major discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Koch discovered the cause of cholera... the discovery should have been immediately followed by numerous official investigations... Hankin's method of prevention by the treatment of wells... should have received close official scrutiny with a view to its general adoption or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When major etiological discoveries are made, governments should initiate official investigations to evaluate and adopt effective preventive/treatment measures rather than leaving them 'sub judice' or ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active official inquiry into modes of propagation of prevalent diseases
rubrics_metrics.description: Typhoid... has never received adequate official inquiry as regards its modes of propagation in that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common and high-burden diseases require targeted official research into transmission modes to inform prevention; failure to investigate is a policy shortfall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage voluntary and unfunded investigations by non-monetary recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: A scientific administration, if it cannot afford to pay for research, would at least attempt to encourage voluntary investigations by such inexpensive methods as promotion, good conduct pensions, special thanks, and recommendations for State honours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where direct research funding is limited, administrations should use promotions, pensions, public thanks, and honours to incentivise and reward investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: State should acknowledge and protect pioneering investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: The public has little sense of the value of scientific investigations, and absolutely no sense of gratitude towards those who carry them out... men have actually suffered for their investigations (examples: King of Madras, Haffkine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governments and public bodies must recognise, credit, and protect researchers; avoid punitive or dismissive treatment of investigators whose work benefits public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary organisation must be scientifically developed and disciplined
rubrics_metrics.description: The people besotted with superstitions, the sanitary organisation insufficiently developed on its scientific side, and the Government knowing nothing of these matters and too weak to exert the necessary discipline, were caught unprepared [re: plague].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective epidemic prevention requires scientifically competent sanitary bodies and the political will to enforce disciplined public-health measures; lack of both leads to catastrophic outbreaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act immediately on validated prevention methods (example: malaria control)
rubrics_metrics.description: We ascertained definitely that the malarial infection was produced by the bites of mosquitoes, and this discovery immediately disclosed several methods of prevention, such as drainage of the breeding pools of the insects, protection from bites by means of gauze, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon validated discovery of transmission mechanisms, authorities should implement practical interventions (drainage, physical barriers, etc.) without delay rather than offering excuses about funds or local conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary departments must perform the tasks for which they are paid
rubrics_metrics.description: One asks why, if the State thinks it worth while to employ sanitary departments at all, it does not see that they do the work for which they are paid?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability: public sanitary bodies should be held responsible and evaluated on their actual execution of mandated public-health duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meritocratic promotion and selection to reduce inefficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Even notorious inefficiency does not always retard advancement, nor even notorious merit accelerate it, with the result that the upper grades are often filled with men of no ideas who have reached their position by seniority, wire-pulling, or even by the mere inertia of their mediocrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative systems should prioritise merit, ideas, and demonstrated public service over seniority or patronage to ensure competent leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education should emphasise scientific method and hard facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Our defective public education... lays too much stress on literary, philological, and dogmatic trifles, and not enough on the hard facts and still harder methods of science, so that the whole nation is tending to become irrational in thought and unpractical in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and public education policy should strengthen training in scientific thinking and methods to produce rational, practical citizens and administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate public expenditure on research (recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: I think that the expenditure on research should reach 5 per cent, of that on all medical and sanitary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a policy target, allocate a meaningful fraction of medical/sanitary budgets to research (author suggests 5%) to ensure knowledge generation that improves efficiency and reduces future costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial cooperation for standardisation (lamp manufacture)
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be admitted that there is still much to be desired; nor does it seem probable that a much nearer approach to perfection is likely to be attained without cooperation between manufacturers and supply engineers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers and supply/utility engineers should coordinate (e.g., on standard voltages and lamp specifications) so that production quality improves and markets are stabilised for better articles at lower price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient sample sizes and representative testing before conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The test results shown by the author are hardly numerous enough to justify the title. Six lamps each from ten British makers is a small number on which to base a condemnation of British methods... a lamp-maker who manufactures four or five million lamps a year may rightly complain on being judged by the performance of a chance six.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical evaluation and public critique of manufactured items require adequately powered and representative tests; avoid drawing broad conclusions from small or unrepresentative samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design lamps to meet specified voltage/candle-power/circuit constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a lamp for a given voltage to have a definite candle-power and take a definite current involves the solution during a difficult manufacture of two simultaneous equations, and the percentage of lamps correctly solving them is small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product specification: lamp design/manufacture must reliably meet electrical and luminous specifications for target supply voltages and currents; engineering and cooperation needed to reduce outfall/variance.
